title: Introduce 'Service Signal Orbit' dashboard and alert elevation rules
author: Aisha Natraj
description:
Motivation: We see recurring noisy alerts during transient token surges and short-lived kernel warmups where cost/latency spikes are high but do not indicate sustained degradation. This PR introduces a new observability surface — the Service Signal Orbit — which provides a compact, multi-dimensional view of short-term health (latency, token-cost, error-velocity, kernel-queue pressure) and a small library of alert-elevation rules that automatically escalate only when signals co-occur on the same invocation cohort.

Summary: Adds a dashboard (Service Signal Orbit) that visualizes per-route and per-tenant 'signal vectors' over rolling windows, a lightweight trace enricher that annotates spans with service_health signals, an alert-elevation rule set that suppresses single-metric flaps and elevates when multiple orthogonal signals align, and a targeted canary rollout for 10% of traffic. The goal is to reduce alert noise while surfacing true cost/latency regressions and token-level hotspots.

Design details: - New metric rollups: error_budget_velocity, burst_score, token_cost_ratio (new tags: tenant_id, route, model_family). These live in metrics_ingest and are exported to the dashboard. - Trace enrichment: telemetry/enrichers/service_health_enricher.go computes a compact bitmask for signals and attaches service_health.tag to spans and logs for downstream correlation. - Alert logic: alerts/service-health-elevation-rules.yaml encodes the multi-signal policy: suppression window + co-occurrence threshold + urgency scoring. - Dashboard: observability/dashboards/service-signal-orbit.json combines sparkline small-multiples, a radial co-occurrence matrix, and a per-tenant token-cost waterfall widget. - Rollout: feature gate + canary policy; config in infra/monitoring/flags.yaml and CI e2e orchestration to flip traffic.

Testing & validation: Unit tests for the enricher and rule evaluator added (telemetry/tests/enricher_test.go). Integration: a synthetic replay with edge-cases was run in CI; initial e2e run failed on a flaky permission race and was retriggered; final run passed. Canary was observed for 48 hours on staging with a 62% reduction in duplicate pager events for bursty kernels.

Operational notes & migration: No breaking API changes. New metrics are opt-in for privacy-conscious Private customers (feature flag). Documentation added at docs/observability/service_signal_orbit.md with guidance on tuning thresholds and rollback steps.

Related: ENG-4427 (reduce alert churn), ENG-4428 (token-cost surfacing), SUP-2211 (customer incident that motivated co-occurrence logic).

review_comments:
Lena Park: Can the enricher be sampled down for high-throughput tenants? Response: yes — added a sampling knob and documented in flags.yaml.
Marco Ruiz: The co-occurrence thresholds look aggressive, will this delay real alerts? Response: tuned thresholds and added urgency scoring to ensure high-severity errors (5xx spikes) still trigger immediate escalation.
Jamal Singh: CI flaky failure reproduced locally; suggestion to add permission retry in e2e. Response: added exponential backoff in e2e runner and reran.
Approvals: Lena approved on 2025-03-01, Marco approved on 2025-03-02.
release_notes: Add Service Signal Orbit dashboard and multi-signal alert elevation rules; introduces service_health trace enrichment and new rollup metrics (error_budget_velocity, burst_score, token_cost_ratio). Canary rollout for 10% traffic and docs included.
